newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso firms slightly at close.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso firms slightly at close.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed slightly firmer at 26.374 to the dollar after some banks sold dollars following heavy flows of foreign funds into the local equities market, brokers said.
The peso closed at 26.375 to the dollar on Friday. The market was untraded on Monday due to heavy rains.
"Some foreign banks were aggressively selling their dollars, but the Central Bank was there at 26.373," one trader from a large commercial bank said.
He estimated that Central Bank bought some $50 million out of the $205.6 million traded throughout the session.
Local shares surged on Tuesday with the key index rising 112.71 points, the second biggest single day jump of the year.
Bankers were buying dollars at 26.366 and 26.365 for value Tuesday, and selling them at 26.374 and 26.375 for value Wednesday to chalk up trading gains.
Another trader said the dollars were also being bid up by some bankers who were anticipating an interest rate cut soon by the Central Bank as the peso-dollar market stabilises.
The peso was threatened last week as regional currencies were hit by speculations following the Thai baht crisis. The Central Bank was forced to raise its benchmark rates.
